subject: Reserved Capacity Options and Activation Trajectory for EmberWorks
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Jules Park <jules.park@emberworks.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity options: preliminary proposal and activation trajectories

Hi Lena / Jules,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great to hear more about EmberWorks' forecasted inference profile and the plan to put model finetuning into production by Q4. Per our conversation I attached a short package (emberworks_reserve_options_v3.pdf) that outlines three reservation constructions we commonly propose for customers with variable launch ramps.

High-level summary (details in the attached PDF + spreadsheet):
- Option A — Compact baseline: 16 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs, reserved 12 months, activation window: immediate (2–4 weeks). Good for tight budgets and early production validation.
- Option B — Standard runway: 64 GPUs reserved with 3-month step-up to full capacity; soft burst credits to cover launch spikes. Balances cost predictability and runway for feature release.
- Option C — Laddered ramp (recommended for your forecast): Start at 32 GPUs then automated tranche increases at 30/60/120 days to reach 128 GPUs by month 6. Includes warm-start credits and a guaranteed min floor during ramp.

Key tradeoffs called out in the doc: min guaranteed GPUs (affects unit price), activation SLA, burst credit policy, and early decommit rules. I also included an activation timeline spreadsheet (gpu_activation_timeline.xlsx) that maps expected traffic milestones to tranche triggers.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Pick the option that most closely matches your expected 90-day ramp profile.
2) Confirm any non-negotiable min GPU floor (this impacts pricing).
3) We’ll provide a final marked-up SOW and DocuSign envelope for signature.

If useful I can schedule a 30-min call with Ben (capacity/product) and Karthik (onboarding/onramp) to walk the activation triggers. Do you have availability this week?

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0198 | tessa.morgan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options: preliminary proposal and activation trajectories

Lena / Samir —

Thanks for the quick review and great questions. Answers below (pulled from the attached doc for convenience):

- Min floor during ramp (Option C): we model a guaranteed reserved floor (billed as reserved capacity) equal to 24 GPUs for the first 60 days to cover baseline traffic and KV-cache population. Above that floor, tranche increases are activated and billed as reserved at the start of the tranche period.

- Acceleration of tranche milestones: standard notice is 7 business days for tranche activation to allow us to allocate warm capacity and pre-warm KV attestation. For emergency immediate bumps we can leverage pre-paid burst credits (subject to availability) but that changes the service-level for warm-cache guarantees.

- Burst credits: tokenized monthly credits in the contract (hours-equivalent) that consume GPU-hours from a quota before switching to on-demand billing. They’re consumed automatically and visible in Console. Example: Option C includes 500 GPU-hour burst credits per month during months 1–3.

Pricing and billing notes (high-level):
- Option A: effective reserved rate = $18 / GPU-hour (estimated committed annualized).
- Option B: $12 / GPU-hour with stair-stepped discounts at each tranche.
- Option C: starts at $14 / GPU-hour for initial floor (24 GPUs), then effective blended rate falls as higher tranches kick in; 24-month commitment recommended to get ladder discounts.

SLA/activation windows: 98.5% uptime SLA for Dedicated pools; activation lead time assumes standard provisioning in our us-west region. Also included are rollback policies if a tranche fails health checks (auto-fallback to previous tranche).

I’ve updated the Drive proposal with these clarifications: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EmberWorks-Proposal-2025 (see /proposal/OptionC-annotated). HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/HW-2025-1134.

I’ll set up a 30-min call with Ben + Karthik and propose Wed 16:30 PT.

Best,

Tessa

Tessa — forwarding my internal notes after reviewing Option C and cost model. Keeping this internal (Ben + Karthik).

Key operational constraints:
- Warm-starting 128 GPUs within 120 days is operationally fine but requires us to reserve a warm pool in advance to hit KV-cache SLAs. That increases committed inventory early, lowering short-term margin.
- We can tighten tranche notice from 7 business days to 3 for a +10% surcharge on hourly rates for the tranche month (to cover rapid allocation and cold-to-warm transition).
- We should push for a 24-month minimum on Option C to preserve the discount bands and protect utilization. If EmberWorks insists on a 12-month term, margin drops ~6–8%.

Suggested commercial tweak to keep deal competitive: offer a 6% one-time signing credit against month-1 invoice if they agree to the 24-month commitment and accept 7-day tranche notice.

If you want I can run a quick model with blended unit economics for 12 vs 24 months before the call.

Ben
Director, Capacity Sales — Redwood Inference

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks — after internal alignment we’re leaning toward Option C (Laddered ramp) but with two asks before we can sign:

1) Hard min GPU floor: we need the contract to reflect a billed minimum of 24 GPUs for the first 60 days (you already proposed 24, please include specific language so procurement can see it).
2) Faster acceleration path: we want the ability to reach 96 GPUs within 90 calendar days (not 120). If you can commit to a 90-day ramp to 96 GPUs we’ll accept the 120-day path to 128 GPUs.

We’re also asking for a 4% platform discount in exchange for a 24-month commitment and a one-time $50k onboarding credit (covers initial ramp support). If that’s feasible please mark it in the SOW and send a DocuSign link — procurement wants to review language around burst credit consumption and rollback windows.

Please include SOC2 AICPA evidence in the DocuSign package or link to your compliance page. We’re aiming to get legal sign-off by 7/25.

Next steps for Redwood: updated SOW with the 24 GPU floor language + modified activation cadence to hit 96 GPUs in 90 days, DocuSign envelope with proposed discounts/credit, and SOC2 link.

If you confirm these, we’ll route to procurement and target signature by 7/25.

Best,
Samir Khan
VP, Infrastructure — EmberWorks
